section_summary.extract_value: This section (2.3 Data analysis) describes data-handling and analytic procedures: missing data imputation using HotDeck Imputation (2.2%), computation of means/SDs/correlations in SPSS v18, model testing with WLSMV in Mplus v7, significance of indirect effects via Sobel's test, and fit-index thresholds/indices (χ2, df, TLI, CFI, RMSEA, WRMR). The section does not mention any study labels (e.g., 'Study 1') nor provide sample characteristics or correlations between body appreciation and BMI.
section_summary.evidence_source: "Prior to analysis, missing data imputation (2.2%) was conducted using HotDeck Imputation (Myers, 2011)."; "Mean, standard deviation, and correlation were computed using SPSS version 18."; "To assess the proposed model, variance-adjusted weighted least squares (WLSMV) estimation was conducted using Mplus version 7."; "The significance of the indirect effect was calculated using Sobel's test (Sobel, 1982)."; "For the WLSMV method, cutoff values close to 0.95 for TLI and CFI, close to 0.06 for RMSEA, and close to 1.00 for WRMR can be considered good fit indices (DiStefano, Liu, Jiang, & Shi, 2018; Hu & Bentler, 1999)."; "To assess the fit of the model, χ2 , degrees of freedom (df), TLI, CFI, RMSEA, and WRMR were calculated (Muthén & Muthén, 2012)." No statements about study numbering or participant/sample characteristics are present in this section.
